title: The film-length box turns red on '60', 'banana', '-5' or '999 min' but never says why, and Run stays clickable
wanted: Tell the first pass I want a 60 second film by typing it
did: Typed 60 (the placeholder reads 'or type: 90 s'), then banana, -5, 999 min, 0 into the 'or type' box in the Re-run first pass panel
happened: Each one just gets a red outline. No words say what it accepts ('60' is red but '60 seconds' and '1:00' work and light up the 1 min chip). The line below keeps saying 'It aims for about 1:30 unless you pick a length' and Re-run first pass stays enabled, so with a red box I cannot tell whether it would run at 1:30 and ignore me.
expected: A bare number means seconds; anything else says 'type e.g. 60 s or 1:30' and Run is off or says it will use 1:30
where: Re-run first pass panel › How long should the film be?
suggestion: Read '60' as seconds; under a red box say what it wants

title: Accepting a waiting first pass after I accepted another AI edit silently threw that edit away (the van shot came back)
wanted: Keep the van shot out (I had just accepted 'cut the van shot') and then also take the new 1-minute first pass
did: With two proposals waiting (my 'cut the van shot' AI edit and the 1-min first pass), Accepted the AI edit (cut 12 shots 1:26), then Accepted the first pass
happened: The first-pass card still said '13 shots 1:35.6 → 14 shots 1:07.8' after the AI edit landed: its 'before' side was the old cut, not the 12-shot cut on V1. Accept gave only 'applied — undo with Ctrl+Z'. The van shot GX010485 is back as shot 5. Nothing warned that the proposal was made before my last change or that it would undo it. Recent proposals lists only the two first passes; my 'cut the van shot' edit is not in the list at all.
expected: When the cut moved since a proposal was made, the card says so ('made before your last change: accepting brings back GX010485') or is rebased
suggestion: Mark stale proposals and list what accepting would undo

title: After I undo an accepted proposal, Recent proposals still says 'accepted' and the '✓ 1 change applied' banner stays
wanted: Know what state the cut is in after undoing the first pass
did: Accepted the 1-min first pass, then Ctrl+Z ('undone: proposal')
happened: The cut went back to 12 shots 1:26 (right), but Recent proposals still lists 'accepted · Re-run the first pass… 14 shots' and the timeline header keeps '✓ 1 change applied ×'. Earlier, reopening the accepted 13-shot pass and discarding it relabelled it 'discarded' although its 13 shots were still my whole film. The labels describe the last button I pressed, not what is in the film.
suggestion: Show 'undone' after an undo; drop the 'change applied' banner when the change is undone

title: 'Open again' on an old proposal after I edited the cut says nothing about my edits since; Accept quietly puts back the shots I removed
wanted: Look at the 1-min first pass again after I had cut the van shot (AI) and deleted shot 2 by hand
did: Recent proposals › Open again on the 14-shot first pass, read the card, Accept
happened: The card's header updated ('11 shots 1:19.7 → 14 shots 1:07.8') and the toast said 'proposal back — Accept or Discard it'. Nothing said it was made before two of my edits or that it would undo them. The Notes still talk about 'the old cut was 95.6s'. Accept: 'applied — undo with Ctrl+Z', and both GX010475 (deleted by hand) and the van GX010485 (cut by the AI on my ask) are back. Only reading the diff lanes shot by shot would have shown it.
expected: 'Made before 2 of your changes: accepting brings back GX010475 and GX010485' or an option to keep my edits
suggestion: On reopen, list the edits since that accepting would undo

title: The 'Working … Stop' button beside the prompt vanishes about 2 s after I press Enter; my Stop click landed on nothing
wanted: Stop the re-cut I had just asked for, straight away
did: Typed 're-cut the whole film to exactly 60 seconds', Enter, then went for the 'Working 0:01 Stop' button beside the prompt (twice)
happened: Both times the inline Stop disappeared under the pointer as the ask turned into a whole-film re-cut: the header switched to '✓ Re-cutting the sequence · Show ×' and the Stop moved to the AI edit card in the Assistant and an × in the top bar. My click did nothing and the job kept running. The ✓ tick in front of 'Re-cutting the sequence' reads as 'done' while it has only just started. (Partly my script's speed: a person needs ~1 s to aim, the button lived about 2 s.)
suggestion: Keep the Stop where it first appeared until the job ends; no ✓ on a running job

title: A click on an empty stretch of track moves the playhead, so my paste landed mid-shot and split it
wanted: Paste the opening shot (cut with Ctrl+X) at the end of the film
did: Typed 10:00 in the timecode (went to the last frame, good), clicked an empty part of V2 to put focus back on the timeline, Ctrl+V
happened: Toast 'pasted 1 shot at 00:00:32:00 — Ctrl+Z takes it back'. The click on empty V2 had moved the playhead to 0:32, so the airport shot went into the middle of GX010494 and split it in two (10 → 12 shots). The toast does say where, which is how I noticed.
expected: Clicking empty track space deselects without moving the playhead (as in Premiere), or paste at the end when I had just gone there
where: Timeline › empty track area / Edit › Paste at the playhead
suggestion: Only the ruler moves the playhead

title: My first trip to the practice project and back wiped Copper's whole undo history (9 steps); later trips kept it
wanted: Peek at the practice bin, come back to Copper and keep undoing
did: With 9 undo steps on Copper (last 'undo: paste a shot'), opened the switcher › starter-bin (first visit: a tour popped up), inserted its clip, switched back to copper-02-2026, Ctrl+Z
happened: ↶ ↷ both grey, tooltips 'nothing to undo' / 'nothing to redo', still the same after F5. The cut itself was intact (12 shots 53.89). starter-bin kept its own 'undo: insert'. Two later round trips (one after a reload, history of 1 and 3 steps) kept Copper's history fine, so it is not every time; I can't tell what made the first one different (it was my first visit to starter-bin, and Copper's history then held AI proposal steps). No message either way.
expected: Undo history survives every switch, as promised, or the switcher warns that it will be cleared
suggestion: Find why the first switch drops the history; if it must, say so in the switcher

title: Asked for 60 seconds; the AI's notes say 'The cut now runs 60.02 s … matches the target' but the proposal is 1:03.4
did: Typed 'make it 60 seconds' in Ask the AI (Sequence scope), waited 40 s, read Notes
happened: Header '14 shots 1:07.8 → 13 shots 1:03.4'. The Notes paragraph says 'The cut now runs 60.02 s, which is 1,439 frames … and matches the project's target.' Only a smaller line after it says 'Boundary polish adjusted 6 of 13 shots … 60.0s → 63.5s'. Neither says 'so it is 3.4 s over what you asked; want me to take it out?'. The big sentence is wrong about the film I'd get.
expected: Notes state the final length, and say plainly when it ends up over the asked length
suggestion: Write the length claim after the polish, or re-trim to hit the ask

title: Stopping a background export with the top-bar × gives no word that it stopped
wanted: Stop the export I had put away with 'Keep working'
did: Clicked the 14×13 px × in the export pill in the top bar ('Stop this render: nothing is written') at 48 %
happened: The pill simply vanished. No toast, no 'export stopped, nothing written' anywhere on screen (the server says 'cancelled — nothing was written'; the dialog showed that sentence when I cancelled from inside it). The × is also the smallest target on the bar, right next to Re-run first pass. At 1280 wide the Next hint shrinks to a bare → while the pill shows (as in round 1).

title: Clicking on a cut between two shots, then Delete, removed a shot at the other end of the timeline; the toast doesn't say which
wanted: Delete shot 2 (the short Spencer shot) near the start
did: Clicked where shots 2 and 3 meet (the edit point lit up yellow), pressed Delete. Happened first by accident while an export ran, then again on purpose
happened: Toast 'removed 1 shot — Ctrl+Z brings it back'. The shot removed was shot 12 (the 9 s GX010495 milk-jug payoff), which I had selected minutes earlier at the far right of the timeline: my click on the edit point lit the edit but did not drop the old shot selection, and Delete went to it. The film dropped from 1:00:08 to 0:51:07; I only noticed because the length changed. The toast names no shot and the scope chip kept saying 'Shot 12 · GX010495'.
expected: A click on an edit point replaces the old selection (Delete then does a ripple on that edit or nothing), and the toast names what it removed ('removed shot 12 · GX010495')
suggestion: Name the removed shot in the toast; clear the shot selection when an edit point is clicked

title: 'Stop' beside the prompt does nothing: the ask keeps running and its answer or edit arrives anyway
wanted: Change my mind and cancel an ask I had just sent
did: Four times: 'look at the pictures: in which shots is someone wearing shorts?', 'look at the frames: which shots show a chairlift?', 'remove shot 4', 'remove shot 5'. Each time clicked the 'Stop' button in the Timeline header (tooltip 'Stop waiting for this ask — nothing changes') 2–15 s in; the last time with a slow press
happened: Every time the 'Working 0:0x' counter kept counting after my click (0:08 → 0:09 → 0:12), no 'stopped' message, and 20–40 s later the result came anyway: the frames answer popped up ('I looked at every shot… A chairlift is in 5 shots'), and the edits arrived as '1 change ready · Review' proposals (12 shots 0:56.3, then 0:54.3). Nothing was applied without my Accept, so no harm to the cut, but the button I pressed did nothing and said nothing. The whole-film re-cut's Stop (on its Assistant card) does work.
expected: Stop ends the ask at once, says 'Stopped · nothing changed' (as the re-cut card does), and nothing arrives later
suggestion: Make the header Stop do what the re-cut card's Stop does

title: A title being designed has no Stop anywhere
wanted: Cancel the COPPER 2026 title while the AI was still designing it
did: Asked 'add a title COPPER 2026 over the first shot', Accepted its 'ask the effect designer' step, then looked for a way to stop while 'Designing an effect — GX010474 — designing the effect' ran (~15 s): the Designed Effects panel, the top-bar pill (hover and click), the timeline banner
happened: Designed Effects shows only a greyed 'Designing…' button and 'Draw a reference'. The top-bar pill is '✦ —— 0%' with no × and no tooltip (the export and first-pass pills have one). The banner offers 'Show', 'Ctrl+Z undoes' and × dismiss. The only way out I found was the ↶ arrow after it had finished; that did remove it ('undo: AI: effect').
expected: The same × / Stop as the other AI jobs
where: Designed Effects / top-bar progress pill while a title is designed
suggestion: Give the design pill an × and the panel a Stop

title: A hand edit to a title's words is not its own undo step: Ctrl+Z after my typo removed the whole title
wanted: Undo my clumsy paste in the title's words ('COPPER 2026COPPER 2026')
did: Designed Effects › edit by hand › words: Ctrl+A, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+V (pasted twice by mistake); the Program showed the doubled words and the check said '✗ a bar cuts across the words'. Then ↶ (tooltip 'undo: AI: effect')
happened: The ↶ tooltip never changed after my hand edit. One undo removed the entire title (effects list empty), not just my typing. Redo brought back the AI's original 'COPPER 2026' — my hand edit is simply gone from history. So the undo arrow can't take back a hand change to a title, and the obvious attempt deletes the title.
expected: Each hand change to a title (words, size, place) is an undo step named e.g. 'undo: title words'
where: Designed Effects › edit by hand / Undo
suggestion: Record hand edits to effects in the undo history

title: Typing 'abc' into the title's y place silently put the title at the very top, half off the frame
wanted: Nudge the title (I fumbled the y box)
did: Designed Effects › edit by hand › place: typed 500 in x (Enter), 'abc' in y (Tab)
happened: x=500 was quietly treated as the centre (fine). 'abc' was quietly read as 0 %: the title jumped to the top edge and is cut off. No 'not a number' message in the box; the only sign is the check line '✗ a bar is cut off by the edge of the frame · Fit to frame' (good that the check exists) while the badge still says ACCEPTED.
expected: Nonsense in a number box is refused and the old value kept, as the timecode box does
where: Designed Effects › edit by hand › place x / y
suggestion: Reject non-numbers in place/size; keep the last good value

title: Typing a path with the focus slipped out of the box still fires a dozen editing keys at once (round-1 CLUMSY-15, unchanged)
wanted: Type a folder path into the switcher's path box
did: Opened the switcher, closed it by clicking its name again (my mistake), clicked where the path box had been, Ctrl+A, typed '/mnt/roughcut/footage/killington-neutral', Enter
happened: No box had focus, so the letters ran as shortcuts: a marker added, In and Out set ('sequence out at 00:00:22:13' is the only toast), the tool switched to Rolling edit (⇹ icon, no message), the timeline zoomed out to 2:00, playback shuttled, and 'g' turned the grade off — the Program now says 'ungraded' in small grey letters. Ctrl+A selected all shots first. I needed the Keys sheet to work out what 'ungraded' meant and had to press V and G, three undos and '\' to get back. Nothing told me the tool or the grade had changed.
expected: A burst of typing outside a text box is caught ('typing? click a box first') or at least tool/grade changes announce themselves
where: Keyboard with no text box focused
suggestion: Toast for tool and grade changes; ignore letter bursts typed faster than a person edits

title: After clicking past the end of the film the Program goes black but still says '6/13 · GX010487'
did: With the timeline zoomed out (from the stray '-' key) clicked an empty spot at about 1:17, past the film's end (1:00:08)
happened: Playhead 00:01:17:04, Program monitor black, yet its label still reads '6/13 · GX010487' as if a shot were there. Black is right for past-the-end, but the label is stale; it should say 'past the end of the film' like the typed timecode does.
suggestion: Label 'after the end (1:00:08)' when the playhead is past the film

title: 'Reject all' on an AI edit can't be undone and isn't listed anywhere; my Ctrl+Z to get it back undid my previous accepted edit instead
wanted: Get back the 'remove shot 2' suggestion I had just rejected (Discard on a whole proposal comes back with Ctrl+Z, so I tried the same)
did: Asked 'remove shot 2', pressed 'Reject all' on its AI edit card (toast 'discarded — nothing changed', header 'Rejected — nothing changed'), then Ctrl+Z
happened: The ↶ tooltip never offered the rejection ('undo: AI: insert + 1 more' before and after). Ctrl+Z said 'undone: AI: insert + 1 more' and silently put the van shot back and pulled out the GX010490 skiing shot I had accepted a minute earlier. The rejected edit is not in Recent proposals (only whole-film proposals are listed), so there is no way back to it except asking again. Same word 'discarded' as for a proposed cut, opposite safety.
expected: Reject behaves like Discard: Ctrl+Z brings the suggestion back, or the toast says 'can't be undone — ask again' and the edit is listed under Recent proposals
where: Assistant › AI edit card › Reject all, then Ctrl+Z
suggestion: Make Reject all an undo step and list AI edits under Recent proposals

title: The AI's 'skiing shot' swap opens on a blue blur blocking the lens; it had said it chose from the written descriptions, not the frames
wanted: Swap the van shot for a skiing shot
did: Asked 'swap the van shot for a skiing shot, keep it 60 seconds', Accepted all (12 s)
happened: It said honestly 'Based on the written descriptions, not the frames' and described GX010490 0.00–4.05 as 'a snowboarder riding under the chairlift'. The shot's first ~half second is a blue pole/glove filling the left half of the frame (the timeline thumbnail is a solid blue block), then snow, a lift tower and fence, with a skier far off. The honesty is good, but it didn't offer to look, and I'd have to scrub every new shot myself to catch this.
suggestion: When it picks a new in-point without looking, check that frame (or offer 'look first')
